body:
_Migrated from issue #1352, filed 2026-08-04._

Found by the v4.1.29 pre-tag refuter gate, against the shipped claim "Saves that fail now say
so, and the reader retries instead of quietly dropping your place."

The server-side half of that fix is real and shipped: a rolled-back write no longer reports
success. The client-side half is weaker than the sentence implies, in three separate ways.

## 1. The classic reader never retries in-session

`cps/static/js/reading/epub-progress.js` `persistCfi` ends at:

```js
.catch(() => { storeCfi(cfi, true); })
```

byte-identical to v4.1.28. It marks localStorage dirty and re-sends **on the next open of the
book**. OBSERVED with `/ajax/bookmark/**` forced to 500: 2 POSTs during page turns, then 0
POSTs across a 20s quiet window. That is recovery-on-reopen, not "the reader retries."

## 2. A failed save is invisible to sighted users

The SPA's retry ladder does work (see below), but when it finally gives up the only matching
DOM node is:

```json
{"txt":"Could not save your reading position.","cls":"sr-only","hidden":true}
```

`useAnnouncer` renders into `sr-only` live regions, and `Reader.tsx:210` states outright that
"the reader has no toast." A screenshot after permanent loss shows a completely normal reader.
The classic reader has nothing at all — no toast, no live region. For a sighted user a
permanently failed save is exactly as silent as it was before.

## 3. The SPA loses the last unsaved position when the tab closes

`Reader.tsx` has no `pagehide`/`beforeunload`/`visibilitychange` handler; its only exit flush is
a React unmount cleanup, which doesn't run on tab close. OBSERVED: turn a page, leave the site
250ms later → 0 POSTs, and SPA localStorage holds only theme/font — no CFI. The classic reader
passes the identical test (2 POSTs via `pagehide` → `flushCfiSave(keepalive:true)`) and persists
`{"cfi":…,"dirty":true}`.

Net effect: the retry ladder extends the window in which the position exists only in a JS ref
from ≤800ms to ≤~14.8s, and across that window the SPA has no durable copy. A page turn during
a failing state also cancels the pending retry (`persistCfi` clears `saveTimer`), so an actively
reading user's retries often don't fire.

**This is not a regression** — before #1316 the SPA didn't write position back at all, so
"can lose the last 15s on tab close" is strictly better than "never saves." It's an incomplete
feature, and the v4.1.29 note has been reworded to describe what actually ships.

## What the SPA does get right (don't undo this)

OBSERVED under forced 500s: `maxInFlight = 1` for the whole run, exactly 4 attempts
(1 + `MAX_SAVE_RETRIES=3`) then stop, real backoff (~2.4s, then two ~9s gaps), rapid page turns
coalesced 4→2, and **every retry re-reads the current position** rather than replaying the
stale one. react-query `retry` correctly not used.

## Fix direction

1. `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` → keepalive flush in `Reader.tsx` (parity with classic).
2. Give the SPA the classic reader's localStorage dirty-CFI durability so the retry window
   isn't memory-only.
3. Surface failure visibly — `sr-only` is not "says so."
4. Either give the classic reader a real in-session retry, or keep its documented behaviour
   and describe it accurately.

Minor hygiene bug found alongside: `flushCfiSave` never nulls `saveTimer.current` when a retry
timer fires, so the unmount cleanup's `if (saveTimer.current)` guard can fire a concurrent
keepalive POST while a request is in flight — a hole in the single-flight guarantee the comment
claims. Low impact (both carry the same CFI).
title: Reader save failures are invisible to sighted users; classic reader never retries in-session; SPA loses position on tab close
